The scorecard is the average of five dimensions, each scored from the platform own pages. Nothing in it is taken from testimonials, ads or the platform self-assigned rating.
whatItClaims: Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
whatWeChecked: The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Open the signup page, enter your information and confirm the account by email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Complete the US$250 deposit to unlock the live dashboard.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Choose your risk level and trading mode, then use the demo to learn the dashboard.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
cons: One figure doing two different jobs.
redFlags: A score and a community mood wearing the same number.
Support figures that contradict each other.
Template placeholders left unrendered.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

faqs.q: Is Trade Flow Pro safe, legit or a scam?
faqs.a: We found no scam indicators in the product, which reads as a functioning AI trading service. The conditions are editorial: claims without verification, conflicting figures and restriction lists that disagree. We rate it safe to research with the conditions in this review.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: The service behind the marketing looks functional, and a careful user can use it without stepping on the fine print.
The scorecard settles at 4.7. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
